review_notes:
I read all of Approximation.lean. It has two theorems, and neither carries a simp attribute. I also read `Wkp.value_restrictL` and `Wkp.iteratedGradient_restrictL` in Restriction.lean, and the statement of `tendsto_normedBumpLp_extendByZero_restrict`.

`value_restrictL` is already `@[simp]`. `iteratedGradient_restrictL` is deliberately not simp. Its docstring says the left-hand side is dependently indexed (`k + 1`) and simp cannot match it, so the file uses `rw`. That is documented and sensible, and I found no competing rules, cycles or unwanted expansions.

The statements' right-hand sides, `Wkp.value k (Wkp.restrictL hU k u)` and its iteratedGradient counterpart, are not simp-normal for the `value` case. This is intentional, because the theorems are stated in terms of the restricted element. I did not find evidence that changing this would improve any use.

I did not run Lean. I found no use of these two theorems elsewhere that would justify a simp-interface change.
